title: Is there a piece of Pompeii in Brazil?
hook: An empress born in Naples brought objects from the towns buried by Vesuvius to Rio.
summary: Yes: Empress Teresa Cristina, born in Naples, brought pieces from Pompeii and Herculaneum that went to the Museu Nacional; the 2018 fire hit the collection, but some was recovered.
cardText: Yes. Empress Teresa Cristina, born in Naples, brought pieces from Pompeii and Herculaneum to Brazil. They were at Rio’s National Museum, and some were recovered after the 2018 fire.

cardBlocks.text: In 1843, a princess born in Naples arrived in Rio de Janeiro, already married by proxy to Emperor Pedro II. In Teresa Cristina’s luggage was a fresco, a wall painting, from the Temple of Isis at Pompeii. Pieces from the towns buried by Vesuvius became part of the Teresa Cristina Collection at the Museu Nacional, Brazil’s National Museum.

Frescoes, bronze jewellery, amulets, glass and oil lamps were on display when the museum burned in September 2018. As teams searched the rubble, items from the collection turned up. That fresco, “Dragon and Two Dolphins”, was found in more than 150 fragments and restored in Italy.
Thanks to Teresa Cristina, Brazil’s National Museum held pieces of Pompeii and Herculaneum; some of them survived the 2018 fire.

deepDiveBlocks.text: The Teresa Cristina Collection, also called the Mediterranean Collection, holds Etruscan and Greek objects and finds from the old Greek colonies of southern Italy, along with Roman pieces, above all from Pompeii and Herculaneum. According to the Italian news agency ANSA, the archaeological collection came as part of her dowry. Historian Anita Correia Lima de Almeida, of UNIRIO, notes that how the collection was formed is tied to the politics of Brazil’s Second Reign.

The objects spent almost two thousand years under the eruption’s debris, were dug up in excavations in the 18th and 19th centuries and ended up in a museum. In 2018 they went back to ashes, this time from a fire. The collection of objects from Pompeii was among the things the museum hoped to recover.

“Dragon and Two Dolphins” is one of the collection’s four frescoes and was painted between AD 62 and 79. The heat, the light and the water used against the fire turned its black background white and warped the fragments. It was restored in partnership with a foundation in Turin and shown in Naples, with its return to Brazil planned afterwards.

After the fire, the Italian government announced it would send pieces from Pompeii and Herculaneum to Rio for a long period, to be shown at the Italian consulate. It also offered help restoring a Greek statuette that Teresa Cristina had brought and that was destroyed in the fire.

claims.text: Teresa Cristina, born in Naples, was Empress of Brazil as the wife of Pedro II.

support.excerpt: As chamas atingiram inclusive uma coleção arqueológica trazida ao Brasil por Teresa Cristina de Bourbon-Duas Sicílias, nascida em Nápoles, como dote de seu casamento com o imperador Dom Pedro II.
Teresa Cristina de Bourbon-Due Sicília, nascida em 14 de março de 1822, na cidade de Nápoles, no sul da Itália, foi uma figura marcante na história brasileira como Imperatriz Consorte do Brasil.

claims.text: In 1843, Teresa Cristina arrived in Brazil married by proxy to Pedro II, bringing a fresco from Pompeii in her luggage.

support.excerpt: Ele foi encontrado em escavações na região e trazido na bagagem da imperatriz Teresa Cristina, em 1843, quando ela chegou ao Brasil casada por procuração com D. Pedro II.

claims.text: The fresco, a mural painting, was part of the Temple of Isis at Pompeii.

support.excerpt: O mural afresco “Dragão e Dois Golfinhos” é um bem cultural que fez parte do Templo de Isis, na cidade italiana de Pompéia, sendo datado entre 62 e 79 d. C.

claims.text: Items from Empress Teresa Cristina’s collection were found in the recovery after the fire.

support.excerpt: Itens de outras coleções arqueológicas, como a mexicana, a brasileira, a pré-colombiana e a da imperatriz Teresa Cristina (1822-1889), também foram achados.

claims.text: The objects lay almost two thousand years under eruption debris and were dug up in excavations in the 18th and 19th centuries.

support.excerpt: Aqueles restos materiais das cidades romanas soterradas pelo Vesúvio em 79 EC, afrescos, joias de bronze, amuletos, vidros, lamparinas e outros objetos da vida cotidiana tinham permanecido debaixo de grossas camadas de material eruptivo por quase dois mil anos.
Resgatados em sucessivas escavações arqueológicas ao longo dos séculos XVIII e XIX e, afinal, musealizados, eles retornavam às cinzas, agora do incêndio.

claims.text: Heat, light and contact with water turned the fresco’s black background white and warped the fragments.

support.excerpt: Devido às altas temperaturas, luminosidade e contato com a água, a coloração negra desse afresco ficou branca e seus pedaços sofreram mudanças físicas, ficando abauladas.

claims.text: The restoration was done in cooperation with a foundation in Turin, and the fresco was exhibited in Naples, with its return to Brazil planned afterwards.

support.excerpt: A restauração do painel de pintura mural “Dragão e Dois Golfinhos” foi realizada por meio de uma cooperação técnico-científica entre a Fundação Centro de Conservação e Restauro “La Venaria Reale”, sediada em Turim, e a equipe do Laboratório Central de Conservação e Restauração (LCCR) do Museu Nacional/UFRJ.
Os resultados da mais recente temporada de restaurações estarão dia 23 de junho, na exposição “Fragilidade e Força”, na Gallerie d’Italia, em Nápoles.
